traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Amazon Web Services Payments manages how money moves between you and Amazon Web Services. It holds the payment instruments you use to pay Amazon Web Services and to receive money from Amazon Web Services, such as cards and bank accounts. It collects payment for your Amazon Web Services invoices, applies your payments and credit memos to them, and returns refunds.

A payment instrument is a channel that moves money between you and Amazon Web Services, and its payment method is the kind of instrument, such as a card or a bank account. A financial record is an invoice or credit memo. It shows how much of its amount is outstanding, processing, settled, and canceled as Amazon Web Services applies payments and credits.

With the Amazon Web Services Payments API, you can read your financial records and account balances, and read your payment instruments and their status.

The Amazon Web Services Payments API provides the following endpoint:

https://payments.us-east-1.api.aws

The amount, in the currency that the records making up this balance were issued in.
The merchant of record that issued the invoices or credit memos that make up this amount.
An amount of the balance that GetAccountBalance returns: the total for one merchant of record in one currency.

The part of the amount that isn't settled and has no settlement in progress. For an invoice, this is what remains to pay. For a credit memo, this is the credit that isn't yet applied. This balance doesn't include processing.

The part of the amount with a settlement in progress, for example a payment that's submitted but not yet confirmed. It moves to settled when the settlement completes, and back to outstanding when the settlement fails. This balance is more than 0 only when the status is PROCESSING.

The part of the amount that is settled. For an invoice, this is the amount paid or covered by credit memos. For a credit memo, this is the amount applied to invoices. This balance is 0 when nothing is settled yet.

The part of the amount that was canceled and isn't settled, for example when an invoice is voided. When a partly settled record is canceled, it keeps its settled balance, and the rest of the amount moves to canceled. This balance is more than 0 only when the status is CANCELED.

How much of the record's amount is outstanding, processing, settled, and canceled. The four balances add up to amount. Each balance is in the currency of amount, and a balance with nothing in it is 0.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to get information about multiple financial records

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Retrieves up to 100 financial records in one request, including the details that are specific to each record's type. Identify each record by its ID or by its invoice ID. Results can be partial: each key that you request appears once in the response, either as a record in financialRecords or as an error in errors. A key that matches no record on your account is returned in errors and doesn't fail the request. This operation provides strongly consistent reads.

To use this operation, you must have Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission for both payments:BatchGetFinancialRecord and payments:GetPaymentStatus.

  • AWS_MARKETPLACE – Products that you bought from sellers in Amazon Web Services Marketplace.

The Amazon Web Services business unit that issued a financial record. A business unit has two parts: the merchant of record, which is the Amazon Web Services entity that issued the record, and the line of business within that entity.

The type of the financial record. The populated member of details matches this type. The following values are valid:

  • INVOICE – An invoice: a bill from Amazon Web Services. Payments and credit memos applied to the invoice settle it.

  • CREDIT_MEMO – A credit memo: a credit issued to your account, for example for a billing correction or a service credit. Applying it to one or more invoices settles it.
The Amazon Web Services business unit that issued the record: its merchant of record and its line of business.
The total amount of the financial record, in the currency that the record was issued in. The amount doesn't change as the record is settled. balances shows how much of it is in each settlement state.
How much of amount is outstanding, processing, settled, and canceled.

Whether the record is open or closed. If you receive a status value that you don't recognize, use this member to tell open records from closed ones. The following values are valid:

  • OPEN – Part of the amount is outstanding or processing. The status is OUTSTANDING or PROCESSING.

  • CLOSED – The whole amount is settled or canceled. The status is SETTLED or CANCELED.

A CLOSED record becomes OPEN again if a payment or credit applied to it is reversed. Its closedAt is then absent until the record closes again.

The settlement stage of the record. The following values are valid:

  • OUTSTANDING – Part of the amount isn't settled, and no settlement is in progress on the record. For an invoice, dueStatus shows whether it's due or past due. The settlementStatus is OPEN.

  • PROCESSING – A settlement of part or all of the amount is in progress, for example a payment that's submitted but not yet confirmed. PROCESSING takes precedence over OUTSTANDING: while any part of the amount is processing, the status is PROCESSING, even if another part is still outstanding. The settlementStatus is OPEN.

  • SETTLED – The whole amount is settled. The settlementStatus is CLOSED.

  • CANCELED – The record is canceled. The part of the amount that wasn't settled isn't collected or applied. The settlementStatus is CLOSED.
The date and time, in UTC, when this record was issued.

The date and time, in UTC, when the record was last closed, that is, when its status last became SETTLED or CANCELED. This member is absent while the settlementStatus is OPEN, including after a closed record reopens.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to get a balance of the account

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Retrieves one balance of your account, selected by balance type, as one amount for each merchant of record and currency. Each amount is the sum of the outstanding balances of your invoices or credit memos that have the status OUTSTANDING. Amounts are never added together across merchants of record or currencies. This operation is eventually consistent. Results are paginated. Use nextToken to retrieve more results.

To use this operation, you must have Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission for both payments:GetAccountBalance and payments:GetPaymentStatus.

accountBalances.merchantOfRecord: Amazon Web Services India Private Limited

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
The balance to retrieve. You can specify only one balance type in a single request. Each balance adds up the outstanding balance of the records that have the status OUTSTANDING. A record that is PROCESSING, SETTLED, or CANCELED isn't included, even when part of its amount is outstanding. The following values are valid:

  • INVOICES_DUE – The outstanding balance of your OUTSTANDING invoices that aren't past their due date, where dueStatus is DUE.

  • INVOICES_PAST_DUE – The outstanding balance of your OUTSTANDING invoices that are past their due date, where dueStatus is PAST_DUE.

  • OUTSTANDING_CREDIT_MEMOS – The outstanding balance of your OUTSTANDING credit memos: the credit that isn't yet applied to an invoice.

The pagination token from the nextToken of the previous response. Omit it to get the first page. Tokens expire. If the token is malformed or expired, or doesn't match the original request, the request fails with ValidationException and the reason INVALID_PAGINATION_TOKEN. In that case, start again from the first page.
The maximum number of results to return in one page. The default is 100. A page can contain fewer results even when more remain. Use nextToken to find out whether more results are available.
The balance, as one amount for each merchant of record and currency. This list is empty when your account has nothing in the requested balance.
The pagination token that indicates the next set of results to retrieve. This value is absent when there are no more results.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to get information about a financial record

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Retrieves a single financial record, including the details that are specific to its type. Specify exactly one of the following:

  • The ID that Amazon Web Services Payments issued for the record, in identifier.

  • The invoice ID that Amazon Web Services Invoicing issued for an invoice or a credit memo, in invoiceIdentifier.

If you specify both or neither, the request fails with ValidationException. If no record on your account matches, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException.

This operation provides strongly consistent reads.

To use this operation, you must have Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission for both payments:GetFinancialRecord and payments:GetPaymentStatus.
The ID that Amazon Web Services Payments issued for the financial record, as returned in id.
The invoice ID that Amazon Web Services Invoicing issued for an invoice or a credit memo. The operation returns the record that has this invoice ID.
The requested financial record.

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Retrieves a payment instrument on your account, including the details that are specific to its payment method, such as a card's last four digits. Identify the instrument by its Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or by its ID. ListPaymentInstruments returns both.

To use this operation, you must have Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission for payments:GetPaymentInstrument. You can scope this permission to the instrument's ARN.

The instrument to retrieve. Specify one of the following:

  • The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the instrument, as ListPaymentInstruments returns in arn. The ARN must be for an instrument on your account.

  • The ID of the instrument, as ListPaymentInstruments returns in id.
The payment instrument, including the details that are specific to its payment method.
The code of the bank that the instrument is registered with.
The name of the bank that the instrument is registered with.
The details of an India net banking instrument. The instrument is registered with one bank.
The suggested number of seconds to wait before retrying the request.
The request processing failed because of an unknown error, exception, or failure. Retry your request.

The invoice ID that Amazon Web Services Invoicing issued for the invoice: the document number printed on it, shown in the Amazon Web Services Billing and Cost Management console and returned by the Amazon Web Services Invoicing API as InvoiceId. GetFinancialRecord and BatchGetFinancialRecord also accept it, as invoiceIdentifier.

Whether the invoice is due or past its due date. This member is present only while the invoice's status is OUTSTANDING. It's absent when the status is PROCESSING, SETTLED, or CANCELED. The following values are valid:

  • DUE – The due date hasn't passed.

  • PAST_DUE – The due date has passed, and the invoice is still outstanding.
The billing period the invoice covers: the period of the usage it bills.
The calendar date by which the invoice must be paid, as the timestamp of 00:00:00 UTC on that day. The invoice is past due from the following day.

The payment terms for the invoice, as Amazon Web Services Invoicing issued them, such as Net30. The due date follows from these terms. This member is absent when Amazon Web Services Invoicing didn't issue payment terms for the invoice.

Whether the invoice was issued once or as part of a billing cycle. The following values are valid:

  • ONE_TIME – A single invoice that isn't part of a billing cycle.

  • RECURRING – One invoice of a billing cycle, such as your monthly invoice.
The details of an invoice: the invoice ID that Amazon Web Services Invoicing issued, the billing period that the invoice covers, its due date and due status, its payment terms, and its frequency.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to list financial records

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Lists the financial records on your account, with the newest first by default. A financial record is an invoice or a credit memo. You must specify at least one record type in types. You can narrow the results further by settlement status and issue date. This operation returns summaries. To get the details that are specific to a record's type, use GetFinancialRecord or BatchGetFinancialRecord. Results are paginated. Use nextToken to retrieve more results.

To use this operation, you must have Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission for both payments:ListFinancialRecords and payments:GetPaymentStatus.

The financial record types to return. The following values are valid:

  • INVOICE – An invoice: a bill from Amazon Web Services. Payments and credit memos applied to the invoice settle it.

  • CREDIT_MEMO – A credit memo: a credit issued to your account, for example for a billing correction or a service credit. Applying it to one or more invoices settles it.

The settlement statuses to filter by. OPEN returns records whose status is OUTSTANDING or PROCESSING. CLOSED returns records whose status is SETTLED or CANCELED. When you omit this member, the operation returns records with both settlement statuses.
The earliest date and time to return records for, inclusive. The operation returns the records that were issued at or after this time.

The latest date and time to return records for, exclusive. The operation returns the records that were issued before this time. When you specify both issuedAfter and issuedBefore, issuedBefore must be later than issuedAfter.
The field to sort the results by. The default is ISSUED_AT, the date and time when the record was issued.
The order to sort the results in. The default is DESCENDING, which returns the newest records first. ASCENDING returns the oldest records first.

The pagination token from the nextToken of the previous response. Omit it to get the first page. Tokens expire. If the token is malformed or expired, or doesn't match the original request, the request fails with ValidationException and the reason INVALID_PAGINATION_TOKEN. In that case, start again from the first page.
The maximum number of results to return in one page. The default is 100. A page can contain fewer results even when more remain. Use nextToken to find out whether more results are available.
The financial record summaries that match your filters, in the requested order. This list is empty when no record matches.
The pagination token that indicates the next set of results to retrieve. This value is absent when there are no more results.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to list payment instrument metadata

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Lists the payment instruments on your account. This operation returns summaries. To get the details that are specific to an instrument's payment method, use GetPaymentInstrument. Results are paginated. Use nextToken to retrieve more results.

To use this operation, you must have Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission for payments:ListPaymentInstruments.

The pagination token from the nextToken of the previous response. Omit it to get the first page. Tokens expire. If the token is malformed or expired, or doesn't match the original request, the request fails with ValidationException and the reason INVALID_PAGINATION_TOKEN. In that case, start again from the first page.

The maximum number of payment instruments to return in one page. The default is 25. A page can contain fewer payment instruments even when more remain. Use nextToken to find out whether more payment instruments are available.
The payment instruments on your account, one summary for each instrument. This list is empty when your account has no payment instruments.
The pagination token that indicates the next set of results to retrieve. This value is absent when there are no more results.

The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the instrument. To allow or deny GetPaymentInstrument for this instrument, use the ARN in the Resource element of an Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy.

The payment method of the instrument. The following values are valid:

  • CARD – A credit or debit card.

  • US_ACH_BANK_ACCOUNT – A US bank account debited over Automated Clearing House (ACH).

  • SEPA_BANK_ACCOUNT – A bank account debited over Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) Direct Debit.

  • UK_BACS_BANK_ACCOUNT – A UK bank account debited over Bacs Direct Debit.

  • IN_NET_BANKING – India net banking. You authorize each payment on your bank's website.

  • CN_BANK_REDIRECT – China bank redirect. You authorize each payment on your bank's website.

  • UPI – Unified Payments Interface, the India real-time payment system.

  • PIX – Pix, the Brazilian Central Bank instant payment system.

  • PAY_BY_INVOICE – Pay by invoice. You pay each invoice yourself, for example by bank transfer, instead of Amazon Web Services collecting payment from a card or a bank account.

The current status of the instrument. The following values are valid:

  • ACTIVE – The instrument is set up, and Amazon Web Services can use it for payments. ACTIVE doesn't confirm that the instrument is verified or that a payment with it will succeed. You don't need to take action.

  • INVALID – Amazon Web Services can't use the instrument for payments, for example because its Direct Debit or UPI mandate is no longer valid. This status is permanent. The instrument doesn't return to ACTIVE. To pay with this payment method again, add a new payment instrument.

  • PENDING_SETUP – The instrument needs an action from you before Amazon Web Services can use it, such as resuming a paused UPI mandate in your UPI app. Amazon Web Services doesn't use the instrument for payments until you complete that action.

  • SETUP_IN_PROGRESS – You completed the setup steps, and setup of the instrument is in progress, for example while a Direct Debit or UPI mandate waits for confirmation. Amazon Web Services doesn't use the instrument for payments until setup is complete. You don't need to take action.
The details that are specific to the instrument's payment method. This member is absent for a payment method that has no additional details.
The date and time, in UTC, when the instrument was registered.
The date and time, in UTC, when the instrument was last changed.

  • ACTIVE – The instrument is set up, and Amazon Web Services can use it for payments. ACTIVE doesn't confirm that the instrument is verified or that a payment with it will succeed. You don't need to take action.

  • INVALID – Amazon Web Services can't use the instrument for payments, for example because its Direct Debit or UPI mandate is no longer valid. This status is permanent. The instrument doesn't return to ACTIVE. To pay with this payment method again, add a new payment instrument.
